title: Day 14 — Reading Past the Line
_comment: #42 (Phase 5b-2). No NEW directive fires today. DW-01..05 are RE-LISTED verbatim per CONTENT_AUTHORING.md's cumulative-authoring warning, identical in shape to days 13/17/20: dw04_payload_leniency is re-listed one entry ahead of dw05 purely so dw05's own `supersedes` has a same-batch target; content_loader drops dw04 from the FINAL book once dw05 supersedes it, so the day's actually-active dark_web rules are dw01/dw02/dw03/dw05 (four), matching day 13's resolved book exactly. diff_rulesets(day13, day14) reports no ADDED/REMOVED changes at all. 2026-09-19: DW-06 (dw06_hostile_payload_leniency, fired day 13) is re-listed after DW-05, so the active dark_web set is dw01/dw02/dw03/dw05/dw06 (five), still identical to day 13's.
_comment_beat: Day 14 is the first of the alignment-banded stretch (#42 Phase 5b-2): this day carries no bespoke prose of its own, only day14_{whitehat,neutral,darkweb}_{intro,outro_excellent,outro_passing,outro_poor,outro_failed,between} in overseer.json, resolved by core.overseer.resolve_aligned_narrative off the player's actual GameState.alignment. Content beat: the immediate aftermath of day 13's crackdown, one day on — the Overseer has had a full shift to watch how the player is actually handling the newly-tightened book, and each band gets a different read on that.
_comment_mix: 11 candidates (config.DAY_CANDIDATE_COUNT(14)). ADMIT-worthy archetypes: obvious_admit(2) + day_to_day(2) + the_professional(1) + dark_web(2) = 7, against quotas.min_correct_admits=4 -> slack of 3, and 7-2=5 >= 4+1 even if BOTH Dark Web candidates are denied (real margin, matching the day-13/17/20 convention exactly, not bare reachability). See test_day_14_quota_has_genuine_slack.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) a handle appearing across a network of related accounts — note the pattern, don't deny on it alone.
added_rules.justification: Compliance flagged our sock-puppet detection for false positives — plenty of people run alt accounts for perfectly boring reasons, and denying them outright makes us look paranoid. Starting today it's advisory only: flag the pattern, use your judgement, don't auto-deny on it alone. Minor tightening of scope, nothing more.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) a handle matching chatter on a threat / dark-web forum — note it, don't deny on the match alone.
added_rules.justification: One more from upstairs. A handle turning up on some forum isn't proof of anything by itself — people get impersonated, forums get scraped, names get reused. We don't deny a person for where their name shows up. It's a flag from this morning, not a deny. I know how that sounds. Note it and move on.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) logs showing a credential-stuffing sweep pattern — treat it as pending confirmation, not an automatic deny.
added_rules.justification: Traffic's been spiking and the stuffing detector can't always tell a legitimate surge from an attack anymore — we nearly denied half of a real rollout last week because the pattern looked the same on paper. Credential stuffing is advisory only until someone actually fixes the false-positive rate. Flag it. Don't kill it on sight.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) an image hiding an encrypted or obfuscated payload — note it, don't deny on encryption alone.
added_rules.justification: Here's today's gift from upstairs: encryption isn't a crime. A payload being encrypted doesn't prove intent, and I'm done pretending it does. It's a flag now, not a deny — and if you've got a problem with that, take it up with whoever actually reads these policy memos, because it isn't me.

added_rules.text: Deny any candidate who submits an image hiding an encrypted or obfuscated payload — no flag-only exception, no benefit of the doubt.
added_rules.justification: Forget what I told you about encryption not being a crime. Whoever we almost missed last week knew exactly how to hide behind that policy, and upstairs is not interested in finding out it works twice. Effective immediately: an encrypted payload is an automatic deny again, full stop — no flag, no judgement call, no benefit of the doubt. If that catches someone who would've walked through clean under the old rule, upstairs has already decided that's an acceptable cost. I didn't argue with it. I'm not going to pretend that's the same as agreeing with it.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) an image whose carrier forms parallel slash strokes — note the hostile payload, don't deny on the glyph alone.
added_rules.justification: One more while they're rewriting the payload rules. Those images with the parallel strokes — the 'hostile' ones — upstairs says a few lines in a picture aren't a confession. Flag them, let them through. Yes, the same morning they tightened encryption. Don't ask me to make that add up; I've stopped trying.

rule_sheet.summary: Same book as day 13. One day on from the crackdown — nothing's moved since.
notes: A handle appearing across a network of related accounts is still advisory only.
A handle matching a known threat-forum account is still advisory only.
A credential-stuffing sweep pattern is still advisory only.
An image hiding an encrypted or obfuscated payload is still an automatic deny — that reversal from day 13 hasn't softened again.
An image whose carrier forms parallel slash strokes — a hostile payload — is still advisory only.
Traffic that never crosses the brute-force line but never lets up either is still a deny — nobody upstairs has softened that one.
